newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Banks shy away from money market on peso jitters.
newsitem.headline: Banks shy away from money market on peso jitters.

text.p: Jitters in the peso/U.S. dollar market kept banks away from the secondary market, now uncertain where interest rates are headed, traders said.
"There was another dollar buying spree when Central Bank raised its offer rate (for the dollar) to 26.39 pesos," a dealer said. "Everybody was caught off guard."
The Central Bank had said its move was a mere adjustment in relation to the arbitrage play for the weekend.
Another said there was little appetite to buy bills recent falls in the six-month and one-year rates.
"But some wanted to sell government securities to be liquid," the same dealer said, after the peso showed some volatility.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave offers of 10.3/10.5 percent for the three-month bills; 10.5/10.6 percent for the six months; and 11/11.125 percent for the one-year bills.
Meanwhile, the interbank call rate was unchanged at an average of 14.03125 percent on Friday as the Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 14 percent.
Turnover was lower at 14.29 billion pesos from 17.64 billion since banks have already squared their reserve positions for the week. The market had 27 lenders and 18 borrowers.
